name: INA219AIDR
title: Zero-drift bidirectional current and power monitor with I2C interface
summary: A shunt monitor that converts both the shunt drop and the bus voltage (0 V to 26 V) and, once calibrated, reports current in amperes and power in watts over I2C or SMBus. It runs from 3 V to 5.5 V at 1 mA maximum, has a programmable gain (±40 mV to ±320 mV), 9- to 12-bit resolution with averaging up to 128 samples, and 16 addresses. The A grade and the tighter B grade come in SOIC-8 and SOT-23-8.
key_figures: ±100 µV max (A), ±50 µV max (B) at PGA = /1
12 bit; 10 µV shunt LSB, 4 mV bus LSB
3 V to 5.5 V, 1 mA max; 15 µA max power-down

circuits.title: Shunt and bus voltage measurement
circuits.description: The minimum hookup. A shunt sits in the line from a supply (0 V to 26 V, 12 V in the example) to its load; IN+ takes the supply end, IN– the load end. The chip reads the drop across the shunt (normally under 50 mV) and the bus voltage from IN– to ground. The chip runs from a separate 3 V to 5.5 V supply, a 3.3 V rail in this circuit, and the two I2C lines are pulled up to that rail. A0 and A1 set the address.

circuits.title: Input filtering
circuits.description: The shunt hookup with a low-pass filter in front of the inputs: a 10 Ω resistor in series with each input and a ceramic capacitor of 0.1 µF to 1 µF across IN+ and IN–. The filter is for transients at harmonics of the 500 kHz sampling rate (above 1 MHz); the same 10 Ω resistors also guard the inputs against fast dV/dt from a hard short.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The general-purpose circuit. A shunt in a 0 V to 26 V power bus feeds IN+ and IN– through RF1 and RF2, with CF across the inputs; this filter is seldom needed, and where its need is unknown RF1 and RF2 are fitted as 0 Ω and CF left off. VS, from 3 V to 5.5 V, has a 0.1 µF ceramic bypass at the pin. SDA and SCL have 3.3 kΩ pull-ups to VS, which can be left out where the bus already has them. A0 and A1 each tie to GND, VS, SDA or SCL to pick one of 16 addresses.

circuits.title: 10 A example
circuits.description: A worked example: a 2 mΩ shunt on a 12 V rail carries a nominal 10 A load (15 A maximum), giving 20 mV across the inputs. The chip runs from 3.3 V to 5 V, bypassed by 10 µF and 0.1 µF. With PGA = /1, BRNG = 0, Current_LSB = 1 mA and Calibration = 20480 (5000h), it reads 11.98 V on the bus, 10.0 A and 119.8 W.

operation.text: A digital current and power monitor. A delta-sigma ADC behind a programmable-gain stage measures the voltage across an external shunt (IN+ to IN–) and the bus voltage at IN– to ground. After a calibration value is written, an internal multiplier gives current in amperes and power in watts, read over an I2C or SMBus interface.

VS is a separate 3 V to 5.5 V supply; the sensed bus can be anywhere from 0 V to 26 V, above VS. Either the bus or VS may be present without the other, so the order of power-up does not matter, and the inputs withstand the full 0 V to 26 V with the chip unpowered.

In continuous shunt-and-bus mode (MODE = 111) the chip converts the shunt voltage, averaging the number of samples set by SADC, then the bus voltage with the averaging set by BADC. Current and power arithmetic runs in the background and adds no time. Other modes convert only one quantity, continuously or once on a trigger. Writing a triggered mode to the Configuration register starts one conversion, even if that mode was already set.

Results can be read at any time; the last conversion stays available. CNVR (bus voltage register bit 1) sets once conversions, averaging and multiplication are complete; it clears when a new operating mode is written (other than power-down or ADC off) or when the Power register is read. OVF (bit 0) sets when the current or power arithmetic overflows, so those values may be meaningless.
Current and bus voltage are sampled at different moments. At 12-bit resolution with 128-sample averaging they can be as much as 68 ms apart.
Power-down cuts quiescent current and stops current into the inputs; full recovery takes 40 µs. ADC off stops all conversions.

The shunt range is ±40 mV at gain 1 and widens to ±80, ±160 or ±320 mV at /2, /4 or /8 (default /8). The bus range is 16 V or 32 V full scale (default 32 V). With a TPS2490 hot-swap controller, whose shunt limit is 50 mV, the 40 mV range shares its shunt below the limit, and /2 (80 mV) covers sensing at or past it.

From power-up the chip converts shunt and bus voltage continuously at 12 bits, with a 320 mV shunt range and a 32 V bus range, so both voltages can be read with no register writes. Current and Power stay at zero until the Calibration register holds a value.

Current and power need Current_LSB and RSHUNT folded into the Calibration register (05h). Bits FS15 to FS1 hold the value; FS0 always reads 0 and cannot be set. The register can also trim out total system error against an external ammeter. Registers are volatile: non-default settings are lost at every power-up.

Registers are 16 bits, sent as two bytes, most significant first. The shunt register is two's complement with a 10 µV LSB; the number of sign bits depends on the PGA setting (full scale 32000 at /8, 16000 at /4, 8000 at /2, 4000 at /1). The bus register holds BD12 to BD0 in bits 15 to 3 with a 4 mV LSB (full scale 8000 at 32 V, 4000 at 16 V). The current register is two's complement. A written register updates 4 µs after the write; above 1 MHz SCL, wait 4 µs before reading the same register back without moving the pointer.

Resolution and averaging can be set separately for the shunt and bus channels and serve as filtering. The ADC samples at 500 kHz (±30%) typical and rejects noise well, except for transients at harmonics of the sample rate (1 MHz and up); an input RC filter handles those. Use the smallest series resistance with a ceramic capacitor of 0.1 µF to 1 µF.

The inputs tolerate 26 V between them, as when the load side of the shunt is shorted to ground. Removing such a short can cause an inductive kick above the 26 V differential and common-mode rating; zener-type transient absorbers with enough stored-energy capacitance handle it. Without large electrolytics near the shunt, a hard short can produce a dV/dt that trips the ESD structures; 10 Ω in series with each input protects against this up to 26 V without hurting accuracy.

Slave only, on I2C or SMBus, through open-drain SDA and SCL with spike filters and Schmitt triggers. Fast mode runs 1 kHz to 400 kHz and high-speed mode 1 kHz to 2.56 MHz. A 28 ms timeout resets the interface if SCL or SDA is held low, so an SMBus cannot lock up. A0 and A1 are sampled at the start of every transaction and give 16 addresses from 1000000 to 1001111.

A write sends the slave address (R/W low), the register pointer byte, then two data bytes, MSB first; each byte is acknowledged. A read uses the pointer from the last write: to change it, write only the address and pointer byte, then issue a START and the address with R/W high; the chip returns MSB then LSB. The pointer stays put, so repeated reads of one register need no new pointer.

The master sends the HS master code 00001XXX at 400 kbps or less; the chip does not acknowledge it but switches its filters for 2.56 Mbps. After a repeated START the protocol is as in F/S mode at the higher rate. Repeated STARTs keep the bus in HS mode; a STOP returns the filters to F/S mode.
Setting RST (Configuration bit 15) or sending an I2C General Call Reset restores the power-up state.
A 0.1 µF supply bypass capacitor, typical, goes as close as possible to VS and GND. Noisy or high-impedance supplies may need more decoupling.

Connect IN+ and IN– to the shunt with a Kelvin (4-wire) connection so that only the shunt's own resistance lies between them; any extra copper carrying the load current adds large error with a low-value shunt. Keep the bypass capacitor close to the supply and ground pins.

15 A maximum, 10 A nominal, VCM 12 V, RSHUNT 2 mΩ, PGA = /1 (40 mV), BRNG = 0. The minimum LSB is 457.78 µA/bit, rounded up to 1 mA/bit, giving Calibration = 20480 (5000h). The bus register shifted right three bits is BB3h (2995), 11.98 V; current reads 10000 (2710h), 10 A; power reads 5990 (1766h) × 20 mW = 119.8 W.
